DecSummary: The worker had numerous compensable and non-compensable accidents and injuries before and after he started working for the employer in 1973.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for back and neck disability after 1991.
The worker's request to reconsider Decision No. 516/94 was denied.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (pensions) (arrears); Pensions (arrears); Reconsideration (Board policy)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a compensable injury in August 1979.  In December 1983, he was granted a .4% pension retroactive to the date of the accident.  In April 1984, it was increased to 2%.  In Decision No. 932/88, it was found that the worker's disability exceeded 2%.  The matter was referred back to the Board.  The Board increased the pension to 10% with arrears to December 1988, the date of a recurrence.  In Decision No. 470/94, the hearing panel granted arrears of the 10% pension to November 1984, the date of an orthopaedic report indicating a disability greater than the 2% that had been awarded by the Board.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 164/94 was denied.  The hearing panel considered the evidence and gave detailed reasons for rejecting the worker's version of the accident.  The worker indicated that he was willing to take a polygraph test, but the Vice-Chair noted that the Tribunal does not use a polygraph when examining witnesses.  All witnesses take an oath to tell the truth.  If a panel finds that it cannot rely on the evidence of a particular witness, it is obliged to provide reasons for not relying on that evidence, as the hearing panel did in this case.

The Vice-Chair clarified Decision No. 351/94 by stating that, in denying entitlement for non-organic disability, the decision was denying entitlement for psychotraumatic disability. It was still open to the worker to seek entitlement for chronic pain.

DecKeywords: Suitable employment; Jurisdiction, Tribunal (Board implicitly dealt with issue); Temporary partial disability
DecSummary: A cleaner suffered a right shoulder injury in June 1992. The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer denying further VR services after the worker stopped a modified work trial in March 1993.

DecKeywords: Investigation by Tribunal (whether required); Reconsideration (consideration of evidence); Reconsideration (dissent)
DecSummary: The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 518/94 was denied. The hearing panel considered the evidence and came to a reasonable conclusion. The fact that one of the panel members dissented did not demonstrate that there was an error in the decision of the majority. The decision of the hearing panel not to obtain a report from a Tribunal medical assessor was not an error, given the evidence that was available.

The reasons for the worker's reconsideration request remained unclear despite requests for clarification from the Tribunal.  There was no bona fide request for reconsideration and therefore it was not considered.  The worker was again urged to obtain representation.

DecSummary: The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Appeal Board denying dependency benefits for the worker's death in 1993.
The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 109/94 was denied. The hearing panel considered the evidence and came to a reasonable conclusion.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 268/94 was denied. The hearing panel considered the evidence and came to a reasonable conclusion. The panel should not have stated that the worker had suffered a non-compensable motorcycle accident. However, there was evidence of some sort of non-compensable incident. The error of characterizing the incident as a motorcycle incident was minor and not a significant factor in the panel's conclusion.
The worker's appeal regarding additional temporary benefits for periods in 1971, 1972 and 1973 was allowed in part.

DecSummary: The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 1052/94 was denied. The hearing panel found that the worker had entitlement on an organic basis but denied entitlement for psychotraumatic disability. There hearing panel considered the evidence and came to a reasonable conclusion.
Since the hearing was adjourned in 1994, the Tribunal has made numerous unsuccessful attempts to contact the worker in order to ascertain whether he wanted to proceed with the appeal.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 215/94 was denied. The worker was informed of the original hearing, attended, gave evidence and argued his case. The Panel could not accept the worker's argument that he was not heard by the original hearing panel.

In Decisions No. 351/94 and 351/94A, the Tribunal granted the worker ongoing entitlement for low back disability and initial entitlement for ankle disability. The Board then assessed the worker for permanent disability and granted the worker a pension for low back disability but not for ankle disability.

In accordance with Decision No. 709/94, the Vice-Chair reheard the worker's appeal and concluded, based on new medical evidence, that the worker was entitled to further benefits for ongoing knee disability.
The worker applied for reconsideration of Decision No. 709/94, in which the hearing panel granted the worker entitlement for chronic pain but denied ongoing benefits for the worker's knee condition.
The worker's application to reconsider Decisions No. 327/94 and 327/94R was denied. The issue that the worker actually wanted to reconsider was in Decision No. 2915/00.
